setup: Print the postcard pages, adult guide page, note situation cards, and revision prompt strips before the writing table opens.
Place pencils, blank scrap paper, and ordinary object idea slips within adult reach so writers can choose one small detail at a time.
Choose a simple recipient role for each note, such as helper, host, coach, tutor, neighbor, relative, or friend, without writing private contact details.
Invite writers to begin with a tiny invented story detail before drafting the real thank-you sentence.
Keep the session screen-free with printed cards, spoken choices, sketches, pointing, dictation, and short written lines.
Prepare one quiet restart page so a writer can switch ideas without explaining why the first draft felt stuck.
coachingMoves: Ask what kind action the recipient did, then help the writer add one invented object or tiny scene detail beside it.
Model one sincere sentence that names the kindness plainly and does not mention value, ratings, or comparisons.
Offer two concrete detail choices when a writer pauses, such as a blue mug or a paper star, and let the writer pick or invent another.
Guide the note through three parts: thank you, tiny story detail, and one warm closing sentence.
Keep corrections gentle by asking what the recipient should picture, hear, or understand more clearly.
Let writers share only a title, object clue, or one sentence if they want adult feedback.
privacyNotes: The pack is printable and offline; it does not need accounts, uploads, photos, recordings, or public posting.
Do not collect mailing details, full names, contact details, child profiles, family records, or private household facts.
Use role labels, initials chosen by the family, or blank recipient lines instead of storing personal identifiers.
Keep finished notes with the household, tutor, or classroom adult; the product does not retain copies.
Stay with ordinary kindness, invented details, and simple objects instead of private adult or family details.
handoff: Send each writer home with the finished postcard draft and one optional revision strip.
Tell adults the note can be completed by pointing, dictating, sketching, or writing one short line.
Suggest reading the note aloud only if the writer chooses, with feedback focused on kindness and clarity.
Remind families that mailing, delivery, or saving the note is handled outside the printable pack.
Offer one next step such as add a clearer object, add a sincere sentence, or copy the final version neatly.
reset: Return unused situation cards and revision strips to the adult folder.
Recycle scrap pages that contain only practice ideas, unless the writer wants to keep them.
Restock blank postcard pages, sharpen pencils, and replace bent object slips.
Write only a nonpersonal supply note if needed, such as more pencils, fewer strips, or extra quiet-start pages.

noteSituations.name: Gift From a Helpful Giver
noteSituations.bestFor: Thanking someone for a thoughtful item without discussing price or asking for personal details.
steps: Name the kind action in simple words: thank you for ____________________.
Invent a tiny story detail about where the object might travel next: ____________________.
Add one ordinary object clue that makes the sentence easier to picture: ____________________.
Finish with one sincere line about how the kindness helped: ____________________.

noteSituations.name: Visit Host Thank-You
noteSituations.bestFor: Writing to someone who hosted a meal, play time, lesson, or calm visit.
steps: Start with the hosted moment using a role label, not private location details: ____________________.
Invent one tiny scene detail from a pretend porch, table, or garden step: ____________________.
Write one real thank-you sentence that names the kindness: ____________________.
Add a warm closing that does not ask for another invitation: ____________________.

noteSituations.name: Tutor or Teacher Help
noteSituations.bestFor: Thanking an adult who helped with practice, reading, math, writing, music, art, or a skill.
steps: Name the helpful action in school-safe words: ____________________.
Invent a tiny story object that could hold the new skill, such as a pencil boat or paper lantern: ____________________.
Add one sentence about what became clearer or easier: ____________________.
Close with a kind line the writer would feel comfortable handing over: ____________________.

noteSituations.name: Neighbor or Helper Kindness
noteSituations.bestFor: Thanking someone for ordinary help while keeping private household facts off the page.
steps: Write the thank-you reason without private schedules, contact details, or family records: ____________________.
Choose one invented ordinary object that could carry the thank-you across a pretend sidewalk: ____________________.
Add one sentence that shows the helper's kindness mattered: ____________________.
Pick a simple closing word or phrase for the postcard: ____________________.

noteSituations.name: Group or Club Leader Note
noteSituations.bestFor: Thanking a coach, club leader, librarian, co-op adult, or activity helper without ranking details.
steps: Name the group moment in general words: ____________________.
Invent one tiny team object, table object, or library object for a story detail: ____________________.
Write a thank-you sentence about patience, planning, kindness, or encouragement: ____________________.
Add one clear line about what the writer appreciated most: ____________________.

noteSituations.name: Surprise Kindness Postcard
noteSituations.bestFor: A short note when the writer remembers a small kind action and wants a quick draft.
steps: Write the kind action in one plain sentence: ____________________.
Add an invented mini-scene where the thank-you rides inside an ordinary object: ____________________.
Choose one feeling word that stays calm and sincere: ____________________.
Finish with a neat final sentence for the postcard front or back: ____________________.

revisionPrompts.title: Kindness First
revisionPrompts.direction: Underline the sentence that says thank you most clearly, then rewrite it with __________.
revisionPrompts.adultLine: Ask which sentence should reach the reader first with __________.

revisionPrompts.title: Tiny Story Detail
revisionPrompts.direction: Add one invented object, place, or small action after the thank-you sentence with __________.
revisionPrompts.adultLine: Offer two ordinary object choices and let the writer choose one with __________.

revisionPrompts.title: Clearer Reason
revisionPrompts.direction: Finish this sentence: I appreciated it because __________.
revisionPrompts.adultLine: Ask what the kindness made easier, calmer, or nicer with __________.

revisionPrompts.title: No Price Needed
revisionPrompts.direction: Replace any value detail with a useful or kind detail: __________.
revisionPrompts.adultLine: Guide the writer toward how the kindness helped, not what anything cost, with __________.

revisionPrompts.title: Better Picture Word
revisionPrompts.direction: Swap one plain word for a clearer picture word with __________.
revisionPrompts.adultLine: Ask which word helps the reader picture the object or moment with __________.

revisionPrompts.title: Warm Closing
revisionPrompts.direction: Add a closing sentence that sounds sincere and simple with __________.
revisionPrompts.adultLine: Offer a calm closing frame such as I hope this note makes you smile with __________.

revisionPrompts.title: Sentence Smooth-Out
revisionPrompts.direction: Read the note softly and mark one sentence to make smoother with __________.
revisionPrompts.adultLine: Read the sentence back exactly once and ask where it catches with __________.

revisionPrompts.title: One Extra Thanks
revisionPrompts.direction: Add one more thank-you detail that is kind, ordinary, and private-detail-free with __________.
revisionPrompts.adultLine: Ask for one small appreciated action, not a full story about the family, with __________.

revisionPrompts.title: Postcard Space Check
revisionPrompts.direction: Circle the best two sentences and copy only those into the postcard space with __________.
revisionPrompts.adultLine: Help the writer choose the two lines the reader most needs with __________.

revisionPrompts.title: Invented Detail Check
revisionPrompts.direction: Make sure the tiny story detail is friendly, invented, and easy to understand with __________.
revisionPrompts.adultLine: Ask whether the detail makes the note clearer without adding private facts with __________.

Tell which sentence should come first on the postcard: ____________________.
